answer: Each epoch the protocol publishes a random umber‑seeded puzzle derived from a sand‑dune hash; every active identity must submit a fresh reasoning trace that fits the puzzle’s logical constraints, and the trace is recorded in a hollow Merkle proof. The verifier checks the trace’s validity and timestamps it, rejecting any identity that cannot produce a unique solution. An attacker therefore must expend the full compute cost of solving one puzzle per fake identity—roughly the GPU‑hour cost of the base model inference—plus lock up a stake equal to the puzzle’s difficulty fee per epoch.
